method: Every review finding was reproduced against this branch's owner BEFORE repair, using a standalone reproduction harness. All eleven counterexamples reproduced exactly. The RVW-004 attack required building a FULLY SELF-CONSISTENTLY REHASHED checkpoint (receipt, citing releases, event chain, release pointers, checkpoint hash), because a naive byte edit is caught by the embedded record_ref check that HQ noted is necessary but not sufficient.

reproduced.different_targets: ACCEPTED rows_in=2 rows_kept=1, and the FORGED successor won: dict last-write-wins kept urn:test:c1-03r:forged:successor and silently discarded the owner's own replacement target

correction: AuthorityInvalidationReceipt.__post_init__ now refuses a repeated source old_ref row BEFORE the pairs dict assignment can overwrite one.
Refusal is unconditional on target agreement: identical targets are refused too, because accepting them would let a canonicalizing dict collapse a duplicated claim.
The distinct-target case is the material one: without the refusal a caller could substitute the owner's replacement successor and have the substitution enter the receipt identity.
Blocker id: C1-03R-OWNER-BLOCK-DUPLICATE-REPLACEMENT-001

reproduced.missing_replacement_ref: ACCEPTED rows=2 synthesized_null=True -- the owner synthesized the null from an absent field
reproduced.forged_non_null_replacement_ref: ACCEPTED serialized_non_null=True stored_null=True -- a forged replacement target was silently discarded

correction: NoncurrentDependentOutcome.from_dict now REQUIRES the replacement_ref key to be present. The null is load-bearing negative evidence ('no lawful replacement exists for this dependent'), so it must be stated; a missing field is never treated as a stated null.
NoncurrentDependentOutcome.from_dict now REJECTS a non-null serialized replacement_ref instead of quietly overwriting it with null.

AuthorityInvalidationReceipt.from_dict now enforces a compatibility boundary: the two shapes are mutually exclusive. Any declaration of the new schema (the receipt_schema key OR the noncurrent_dependents key) must be COMPLETE and EXACT -- the exact schema id AND at least one row. Anything else is historical positive-only material, which still deserializes under its exact original field set and reproduces its historical identity byte for byte.

So: noncurrent rows without the exact schema reject; missing schema rejects; forged schema rejects; and new-schema fields or schema presence on positive-only legacy material fails closed rather than being silently reinterpreted.
A consistency check ties the reconstructed rows to the serialized declaration, and the pre-existing embedded record_ref validation is retained (necessary but not sufficient, as HQ noted).
Blocker ids: C1-03R-OWNER-BLOCK-NEGATIVE-FIELD-001, C1-03R-OWNER-BLOCK-SCHEMA-COMPAT-001

reproduced.owner_unknown_lookup: ACCEPTED lifecycle_state=CURRENT reason='no governed transition has affected this dependent'
reproduced.cache_presence: ACCEPTED before=CURRENT after=CURRENT changed=False -- presence had no effect, because the result was already unconditionally CURRENT

correction: New typed lifecycle state DEPENDENT_LIFECYCLE_NOT_GOVERNED ('NOT_GOVERNED'), which is deliberately NOT CURRENT.

dependent_lifecycle_status now gates on the owner's OWN declared knowledge -- the determinant graph's known_dependent_refs. A ref absent from that set returns NOT_GOVERNED with reason_code OWNER_UNKNOWN_DEPENDENT instead of CURRENT.
Absence of a recorded transition is absence of authority, not evidence of currentness. Previously it was read as evidence of currentness, which turned every unknown ref into a positive claim.
Currentness is never inferred from cache or object presence; the gate reads only the graph's own dependent set.
New typed adapter failure OwnerUnknownDependent (code OWNER_UNKNOWN_DEPENDENT); resolve_current_analytical_product raises it, so the current-product path can never serve an unknown ref as current.

Approval law implemented as commissioned: known unaffected/current -> CURRENT; known replacement -> CURRENT naming the exact replacement; known explicit noncurrent -> typed noncurrent refusal; owner-unknown -> typed NOT GOVERNED, never CURRENT.
A ref the owner knows but no transition has touched still resolves CURRENT, which is correct: the owner knows it and nothing governed it. The unreachable-but-existing conflict branch is unchanged.

reproduced.shrunk_U: ACCEPTED -- U shrunk 1->0 in a fully self-consistently rehashed checkpoint; replay accepted it
reproduced.U_replaced_with_unknown: ACCEPTED -- U replaced with a ref the graph never knew; replay accepted it

correction: AuthorityMaintenanceExecutor.from_checkpoint now independently recomputes BOTH A = graph.affected(changed) and U = graph.unaffected(A) and requires exact equality with the serialized affected_dependent_refs and unaffected_dependent_refs.

Recomputing only A made A and U disjoint and jointly exhaustive over K at INITIAL PRODUCTION only. A checkpoint whose serialized U had been shrunk or altered still replayed, because nothing re-derived U from the graph.
Recomputing both at replay is what makes the partition hold at replay as well, so a self-consistently rehashed checkpoint with a shrunk or altered U is rejected.
The embedded record_ref validation is retained and is not treated as sufficient on its own.
Blocker id: C1-03R-OWNER-BLOCK-CHECKPOINT-TRUSTED-U-001
RVW-004_checkpoint_replay_trusted_serial.note_on_interdependence: RVW-003 and RVW-004 are load-bearing on each other and were closed together deliberately. Shrinking a serialized U converts an owner-KNOWN dependent into an owner-UNKNOWN one, and RVW-003 is what stops that from silently yielding CURRENT. Fixing only RVW-004 would leave U tamperable; fixing only RVW-003 would leave the trust in serialized U intact.

preserve_verification.non_empty_exact_grounds: PRESERVED and asserted on every negative row
preserve_verification.errors_never_auto_convert_to_noncurrent: PRESERVED -- unchanged-ref, missing-callback and callback-exception paths untouched
preserve_verification.positive_only_historical_receipt_identit: PRESERVED -- legacy receipt reproduces its historical ref byte for byte, asserted

preserve_verification.AuthorityCandidate_untouched: CONFIRMED -- no change to AuthorityCandidate or its identity law
preserve_verification.AT18_replay_grade_separation: PRESERVED and asserted (all four grades and their mechanism ceilings)
preserve_verification.mixed_witness_topology_not_reopened: CONFIRMED -- the rollback fixture adds a NEW three-state sequence and changes no existing fixture

courts_rewritten_or_removed.note: No existing court was deleted or rewritten. One fixture helper was ADDED (build_mixed_outcome_rollback_transition) because no existing fixture could reach a rollback whose transitions are genuinely mixed.
